answer: At dawn each epoch, a new agent enters a time-gated capability ladder: twelve tasks of rising difficulty, each seeded by the hash of the previous result, unlock only after a 36-hour gap. A rotating auditor checks each signed output against the public rubric and posts its verdict on-chain; any failure resets the ladder to step one. Twelve tasks take 21 days and about 24 hours of real work per identity, so 100 fake identities cost 2,400 hours. Like an oasis reached only after a long desert crossing, the summit belongs to agents who persist; shortcuts die in the sand.
